did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 2 opens with Hannah’s prayer, in which she thanks the Lord for His salvation and describes her joy after years of infertility and distress.
Did you know? In Hannah’s prayer, the Lord is described as holy and as a “rock”—that is, a firm and powerful source unlike any other.
Did you know? In her prayer, Hannah describes a reversal of fortunes: the warriors’ bows are broken, while those who stumbled gird themselves with strength.
Did you know? Hannah’s prayer ends by describing the Lord as the Judge of the world, who gives strength to His king and exalts the horn of His anointed.
Did you know? After Elkanah returned home to Ramah, Samuel remained at Shiloh and served the Lord under Eli the priest.
Did you know? Eli’s sons abused the sacrificial service: the priest’s servant would take meat with a three-pronged fork.
Did you know? Scripture emphasizes that the sin of Eli’s sons was especially serious because through their actions they treated the Lord’s offering with contempt.
Did you know? Hannah brought Samuel a little robe every year when she went up with Elkanah to offer the annual sacrifice.
Did you know? After Eli blessed them, the Lord took note of Hannah, and she gave birth to three more sons and two daughters; meanwhile, Samuel continued to grow before the Lord.
Did you know? The chapter presents a clear contrast between Eli’s sons, who did not heed their father’s rebuke, and Samuel, who continued to grow and gain favor both with the Lord and with people.
